title: ANDS Studio overall product concept
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar branded "ANDS Studio" and the subtext "· guided ANDS filing", plus chips for "Help", "My dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry" and "Correspondence". The hero headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." Below it, body copy states: "An Abbreviated New Drug Submission is one of the most complex filings a company can make. This walks you through it step by step — every term explained in plain language with the regulatory vocabulary kept precise, the right pathway chosen for your product, and your submission's readiness visible at every moment until it's ready to send." The main button is "Start my submission →", with a secondary link "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →" and a footnote: "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

Clicking "Start my submission →" opens a three-column layout: a step rail of journey stages on the left, the active step's card in the middle, and a right-hand panel showing a 3D "submission tower" of module tiles plus a readiness card. The top bar now shows a readiness chip — either "Ready to file" or a percentage like "34% ready" — and a "Start over" button. Returning later resumes your saved session ("Loading your filing…").

On the "Account & security" page, the product surfaces its operations posture. It states ANDS Studio is self-hosted: every service and database runs inside your own environment, and nothing leaves it except the packages you deliberately transmit to Health Canada. Every record is scoped to this workspace at every service, and cross-workspace reads are refused at the API, not just hidden in the UI. You can add a time-based one-time code (TOTP) from a standard authenticator app as a second factor via "Set up authenticator app →". The page also records honest limits: single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) is not yet available — accounts are per-workspace — and every state change lands on an append-only audit event stream.

Choosing "My dossiers" instead shows "Your product dossiers" with a "New dossier +" button. If empty: "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." Creating one asks for "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). You must know the ID format: entering anything else yields "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". Helper text explains Health Canada issues the ID via a REP request through your CESG account, and offers "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →", which generates a d-prefixed draft ID. "Create & open →" drops you into that dossier's Module 1 workspace.

Inside a dossier, the top bar swaps to tabs M1–M5 with pass/todo/not-applicable markers, plus chips "Application Viewer", "Audit", "Portfolio" and "Journey" to hop back to the guided flow.
